purpose: Teach: 声援/町民/趙/マメ/穂/山々/見所/７つ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが選手達に大きな声援を送られた
lines.en: Gran, when Dad was young, he used to cheer the players on with such a big voice.
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic tone. Gentle opening, as if reaching back into memory. Slow, careful pacing — savoring the detail. Warm and slightly distant, like holding something precious from long ago.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、町民会の役員されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and you, dear — you used to be quite the town council member back in those days, didn't you?
lines.style: Bright and knowing, gently teasing. A warm half-laugh underneath. The affectionate ease of someone who knows exactly what he was like then. Light, playful rhythm — turning his memory back on him with love.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが中国出張で趙氏と懇意になられた
lines.en: Gran, when Dad was young, he grew close to someone named Zhao during his business trip to China.
lines.style: Quieter now. Reflective, almost wondering. A slight pause before the name, as if bringing it forward carefully from memory. Tender but deliberate — the voice of someone speaking of connections that mattered.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、マメに日記を付けられたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you, dear — you were so diligent keeping that diary all those years, weren't you?
lines.style: Warm surprise and gentle pride. A small knowing laugh at the memory. Not teasing this time — genuinely admiring. Steady, steady rhythm, as if counting through those years along with him.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが田んぼの穂、つまり稲穂を眺められた
lines.en: Gran, when Dad was young, he used to stand and gaze at the rice ears in the paddies.
lines.style: Very quiet and present. A long, tender opening on the image. Slow enough to linger. The voice of someone who can still see it — what he saw. Trailing softly into the rice fields, half-remembering, half-honoring.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、信州の山々を巡られたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you, dear — you walked through those mountains in Shinshu all those times, didn't you?
lines.style: Brighter, more energetic than before. The lift of shared adventure and movement. A smile in the voice — seeing him younger, more restless. Rhythmic and spirited, almost playful, as if walking beside him through those paths.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが「我が庭の見所は紅葉」と仰った
lines.en: Gran, when Dad was young, he used to say, 'The finest thing about our garden is the autumn leaves.'
lines.style: Quietest yet. Reverent, almost quoting something sacred. A long, gentle pause before the quote itself. Deep respect in the delivery — as if those words are still living. Slow, measured, each phrase like a gift being placed down carefully.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、お孫様に７つの教えを残されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you, dear — you passed on seven teachings to our grandchildren in those days, didn't you?
lines.style: Warm, deep with quiet pride. Slower tempo, honoring what was given. A hint of emotion under the surface — not quite sorrow, but the weight of legacy and time. Gentle closing, like settling something important into place. Close to him, intimate and sure.
